Jarrett Matthew Jack (born October 28, 1983) is an American.
Jack is a professional basketball coach and former player.
Jack is an assistant coach for the Detroit Pistons of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Jack attended four high schools: DeMatha Catholic High School, St. Vincent Pallotti High School in Maryland, Mount Zion Academy in North Carolina, and Worcester Academy in Massachusetts.
Jack was considered a four-star recruit by Scout.com.
Jack was listed as the No. 9 point guard and the No. 40 player in the nation in 2002.
Jack played for Georgia Tech in Atlanta.
In Jack's sophomore year (2003–04), he helped guide Georgia Tech to the NCAA Finals with 12.5 points and 5.1 assists per game.
In Jack's junior and final year at Georgia Tech, he averaged 15.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.5 assists.
Jack graduated on December 13, 2014, receiving his degree in business management from Georgia Tech.
Jack was selected with the 22nd overall pick in the 2005 NBA draft by the Denver Nuggets.
On draft night, Jack was traded to the Portland Trail Blazers for their 27th and 35th picks (Linas Kleiza and Ricky Sánchez).
As a rookie in 2005–06, Jack backed up Steve Blake and Sebastian Telfair as a point guard.
In 2006 off-season, Jack was named starting point guard by coach Nate McMillan for the 2006–07 season.
Jack's minutes and stats increased dramatically in the 2006–07 season due to the absence of Blake.
With Blake's return in 2007–08, Jack was once again relegated to sixth man.
On July 9, 2008, Jack was traded to the Indiana Pacers along with Josh McRoberts and Brandon Rush for Ike Diogu and Jerryd Bayless.
On July 13, 2009, Jack signed a 4-year, $20 million offer sheet with the Toronto Raptors.
The Pacers had seven days to match the offer, but they chose not to.
On November 20, 2010, Jack was traded to the New Orleans Hornets along with Marcus Banks and David Andersen for Peja Stojaković and Jerryd Bayless.
On July 11, 2012, Jack was traded to the Golden State Warriors in a three-team trade including the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics.
Jack recorded a double-double with 30 points and 10 assists against the Spurs on February 22, 2013.
At the end of the season, Jack finished third in the Sixth Man of the Year voting.
On July 12, 2013, Jack signed with the Cleveland Cavaliers.
On April 15, 2014, Jack was named the recipient of the ninth annual Austin Carr Good Guy Award.
On July 10, 2014, Jack was traded to the Brooklyn Nets along with Jerryd Bayless and Edin Bavčić in a three-team trade involving the Boston Celtics and Cleveland Cavaliers.
Jack travelled to Charlotte on December 13, 2014, after graduating from Georgia Tech to join his teammates for their game against the Hornets.
In 20 minutes of action off the bench, Jack recorded 14 points, 5 assists, and 2 rebounds in a win over the Golden State Warriors on November 14, 2015.
Jack was ruled out for the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament and small medial meniscus tear in his right knee on January 3, 2016.
On June 30, 2016, Jack was waived by the Brooklyn Nets.
On July 15, 2016, Jack signed with the Atlanta Hawks.
On October 20, 2016, Jack was waived by the Atlanta Hawks due to injury.
Jack had a torn right knee ligament in 2015–16 that prevented him from practicing during training camp and sitting out all seven of the Hawks' exhibition games during the preseason.
On February 24, 2017, Jack signed a 10-day contract with the New Orleans Pelicans for a second stint.
On March 3, 2017, Jack was ruled out for four to six weeks after suffering a right lateral meniscus tear.
On September 15, 2017, Jack signed with the New York Knicks.
On November 24, 2017, Jack had 10 points and a season-high 14 assists against the Atlanta Hawks.
On December 10, 2017, Jack scored a season-high 19 points against the Atlanta Hawks.
On January 10, 2018, Jack recorded his first triple-double in six years with 16 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a double overtime loss to the Chicago Bulls.
Four days later, on January 14, 2018, Jack set a new season high with 22 points in an overtime loss to the New Orleans Pelicans.
Jack signed with the New Orleans Pelicans on September 19, 2018, before being waived on October 13.
On March 5, 2019, Jack was acquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce of the NBA G League.
In his lone appearance for the Skyforce, Jack tore the ACL and lateral meniscus in his left knee as well as spraining the MCL, ruling him out for the rest of the season.
On November 26, 2019, Jack was acquired again by the Sioux Falls Skyforce.
Jack signed with the NBA G League Ignite on January 14, 2021.
Jack was hired as an assistant coach for the Phoenix Suns on August 7, 2021.
Jack was hired as an assistant coach for the Detroit Pistons on June 16, 2023.
Chris Duhon is Jack's cousin.
